articles.headline: Inside the stunning 72-hour Lakers sale -- and the uncertainty that still looms
articles.description: Three days of secret talks resulted in Mark Walter flipping the Lakers -- and reignited yet another round of bickering among the six Buss siblings.

images.name: Lakers [1296x729]
images.caption: The summer sale of the Lakers sent shockwaves across the sports world, and sent the organization into chaos -- again.
images.credit: AP Photo, Getty Images, Imagn Images

images.name: Shelburne Lakers sale -- photo2 [576x324]
images.caption: When Jeanie Buss sold the Lakers to Walter, she showed Doncic paperwork that assured him that she would still be in charge of his basketball future. Ten months later, that promise is no longer certain.

images.name: Shelburne Lakers sale -- photo3 [576x324]
images.caption: The second sale of the Lakers put the team in significant transition again -- with new owners evaluating everything and squabbling former owners jostling for power and money. Iger and Kushner are Doncic's fifth team owners in the past three years.

articles.description: In his fourth game, Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg put up 31 points, 12 rebounds and six assists in a blowout road win over the Nuggets on Monday night.

images.name: Yaxel Lendeborg [600x400]
images.caption: "He's as strong as an ox and skilled," Warriors coach Steve Kerr said of Yaxel Lendeborg. "You saw tonight. In all the critical moments of the game, we just put the ball in his hands. For a rookie to be that advanced already, it's extremely rare."

article.story: CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- — Brandon Miller scored 34 points and the Charlotte Hornets beat the winless Miami Heat 115-110 on Saturday, bouncing back from one of the worst losses in franchise history a night earlier. Charlotte’s 128-81 loss to Atlanta on Friday in its home opener was the fifth-largest in franchise history. Miller missed 12 of 14 field goal attempts and 10 of his 11 3-point tries in a six-point effort that came four days after he had signed a five-year, $209 million contract extension. Dennis Schroder added 25 points, Naz Reid had 23 and Grayson Allen 20 for Charlotte (2-1). Giannis Antetokounmpo was limited to 14 points — more than 20 fewer than the 35.5 per game he averaged in his first two games after his trade from the Milwaukee Bucks in one of the biggest NBA offseason transactions. The Hornets, who were 11 of 51 from 3-point range Friday, made 16 of 43 on Saturday. Five of those 3s sparked a 24-7 run in the third quarter that gave them control of the game to the delight of the sellout crowd of 19,611 at Spectrum Center. Leading 68-63 with 10 1/2 minutes left in the third period, Charlotte’s surge gave it a 92-70 advantage with 2:55 left in the quarter. But with Antetokounmpo in foul trouble — he would foul out with 1:57 to play — Miami coach Erik Spoelstra used a lineup of starters Davion Mitchell and Bam Adebayo and reserves Pelie Larsson, Tim Hardaway Jr. and Bobby Portis Jr. to spark a rally that forged ties at 100, 102 and 104. After the final tie with 3:46 to play, Allen turned the momentum back Charlotte’s way for good with an acrobatic 3-pointer from the left wing while being fouled by Hardaway at the end of the 24-second shot clock. When Allen’s free throw completed the four-point play, it gave Charlotte a 108-104 lead. Miami would not get any closer than three the rest of the way. Mitchell led Miami with 22 points with Adebayo adding 20, Larsson 15 and Klay Thompson 14. The teams were meeting for the first time since Charlotte's 127-126 overtime win in the Eastern Conference play-in tournament ended Miami’s 2025-26 season. Charlotte’s LaMelo Ball, who hit the game-winning shot in that victory, was traded to the Minnesota Timberwolves in the offseason. Up next Heat: Host Dallas on Monday. Hornets: Host Washington on Monday.
